# Directories that cannot be projects

<!-- GENERATED by `just disallowed-doc` from internal/monitor/disallowed_paths.go — do not hand-edit -->

Endless refuses to register, auto-register, or resolve a project at certain
directories. Every registration path applies the same rules: the hook's
auto-registration, `endless project register`, discover and reconcile.

- **self** — the directory itself can never be a project; a directory inside it can.
- **subtree** — neither the directory nor anything inside it can be a project.
- **parent directory** — not a project itself, and the search for an enclosing
  project stops there, so nothing inside inherits a project registered above it.

## Always refused

`$HOME` itself, and every directory above it (`/Users`, `/home`, `C:\Users`, `/`),
scope **self**. This cannot be overridden. Directories outside `$HOME` (such
as `/work/app` in a container) are allowed.

A project nested inside another registered project is also refused, in either
direction.

## Overrides

Add or remove entries in `~/.config/endless/disallowed-paths.json`, which Endless
creates empty the first time it needs it. It holds only your changes, so new
built-in entries in a later Endless still reach you:

```json
{
  "add": [
    {"path": "~/Scratch", "scope": "subtree"},
    {"path": "~/Code", "parent_dir": true}
  ],
  "remove": ["/etc"]
}
```

A directory can also declare itself a parent directory with a `.endless-parent-dir`
file, or opt out entirely with `.endless-ignore`.

User folders such as Downloads are found where the OS keeps them: on Linux
from `~/.config/user-dirs.dirs` (so localized names work, and servers
without the file skip them), on Windows from the known-folder API (so a
relocated folder still matches), and on macOS at their fixed English names.

## macOS

| Directory | Scope | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `/System` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/Library` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/Applications` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/bin` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/sbin` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/usr/bin` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/usr/sbin` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/usr/lib` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/usr/libexec` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/usr/share` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/dev` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/cores` | subtree | operating-system files |
| `/private` | subtree | operating-system files and temporary files (/etc, /tmp and /var resolve here) |
| `~/Library` | subtree | application data and settings |
| `~/Applications` | subtree | application data and settings |
| `~/.Trash` | subtree | application data and settings |
| `~/Downloads` | subtree | downloads or media, not code |
| `~/Music` | subtree | downloads or media, not code |
| `~/Pictures` | subtree | downloads or media, not code |
| `~/Movies` | subtree | downloads or media, not code |
| `/usr` | self | a mount point; its children may be projects |
| `/usr/local` | self | a mount point; its children may be projects |
| `/opt` | self | a mount point; its children may be projects |
| `/Volumes` | self | a mount point; its children may be projects |
| `~/Desktop` | self | a user folder; its children may be projects |
| `~/Documents` | self | a user folder; its children may be projects |
| `~/Public` | self | a user folder; its children may be projects |
| `~/Projects` | parent directory | a folder of projects |
